subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should OpenClaw accept native Siri/Shortcuts ask-and-spoken-reply support, and which authorized Gateway boundary should it use?
rationale: The request changes who may initiate agent work from Siri/Shortcuts and how session and reply routing are authorized; current code shows multiple possible boundaries but no approved contract.

options.title: Approve paired-node App Intent design
options.body: Implement Siri/Shortcuts on top of the existing paired iOS node/operator identity and chat/session routing so it inherits existing Gateway trust controls.

options.title: Use a hardened hook boundary
options.body: Permit a /hooks/agent-style implementation only with explicit hook-token storage, session/agent allowlists, idempotency, and local confirmation rules.

options.title: Defer native ask-and-reply
options.body: Keep Shortcuts plus webhook and the Talk Mode launch path as the supported workaround until maintainers prioritize the full Siri surface.

recommendation.title: Approve paired-node App Intent design
recommendation.body: Implement Siri/Shortcuts on top of the existing paired iOS node/operator identity and chat/session routing so it inherits existing Gateway trust controls.

likelyOwner.reason: The iOS app scaffold, AppIntents framework link, and much of the sampled iOS app history trace to this owner path.
